behavior: Accumulate exact encoding-boundary buffer payload, texture source bytes, row padding, scatter index bytes, staging capacity, buffer copy bytes/count, texture copy count and scatter dispatch count. Publish only after queue submission at the common Batch hold boundary. Refused and cancelled batches contribute zero. Production screen streams share the 16 MiB GPU allowance, so retained snapshot payload is at most 32 MiB per renderer plus allocation headers; this replaces the former 4.5 MiB bound for nine 256 KiB double snapshots. Trim obsolete prepared capacity after shrink; release both snapshots when an uncached control buffer retires. Construction peaks, prepared source geometry and dirty-range metadata are separate.

Exact dirty comparisons now cover large admitted buffers. Preserve separate submitted/prepared baselines, cancellation, sparse scatter and hard GPU budgets. Oversized uncached control allocations still require fresh upload by CTL-02 design.

limits: Totals are renderer-owner cumulative submission observations, not GPU execution or per-consumer/frame classifications. Texture padding describes staging footprint, not texture pixel payload; mapped capacity and scatter packet capacity are not additional logical payload. Readback and device-internal work remain outside upload totals.

Larger retained CPU snapshots trade memory for exact large-screen reuse. Full T1 RSS/peak and scale qualification, pending-range metadata, CPU construction/transient accounting and all required S5 scenarios remain open.

No complete REUSE-SCREEN/MEM-01/ACC-01, S4/S5 or issue acceptance. Preserve GEFN, nonblocking resize and concurrent multi-device boundaries. No dependency, vendoring, prototype, numerical specification cap or licensing change.
